findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is stored in the EC2 metadata service and visible to anyone with API/console access or read access to the instance metadata, resulting in credential leakage.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, TLS termination), exposing the web service in cleartext to the entire internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume is not encrypted at rest, risking exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption specified, so the snapshot itself is unencrypted and could expose sensitive data if the snapshot is shared or leaked.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet (such as the web_host instance with an open SSH port) to automatically receive public IPs, increasing internet-facing attack surface.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing any instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IPs, increasing internet-facing attack surface unnecessarily.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to and disclosure of network traffic metadata.
